examples.ko: 그분은 끝내 고국에 돌아오지 못하고 이국땅에 묻혔어요.
examples.en: He never made it back to his homeland and was buried in a foreign land.

examples.ko: 이국땅에서 혼자 살다 보니 가족이 정말 그리워요.
examples.en: Living alone in a foreign land, I really miss my family.
My first Lunar New Year in a foreign land was lonely.

examples.ko: 말이 안 통하는 이국땅에서 길을 잃어 당황했어요.
examples.en: I got lost in a foreign land where I couldn't speak the language, and I panicked.
I saw off my friend at the airport as he left for a foreign land.

examples.ko: 이국땅에서도 한국 음식을 먹으면 힘이 나요.
examples.en: Even in a foreign land, eating Korean food gives me energy.

explain: '외국'보다 쓸쓸함이나 그리움 같은 감정이 담겨요. 고향을 떠나 사는 사람의 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 짝이 되는 말은 '고국'이나 '고향'이에요. 단순히 외국 여행을 말할 때는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: I'm living alone in a foreign land.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고향을 떠나 외국에서 사는 외로움이 담긴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries the loneliness of living abroad away from home.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a foreign land

phrases.en: It was my first winter in an unfamiliar foreign land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낯선'을 붙여 처음 와서 어색한 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 낯선 emphasizes the unfamiliar feeling.

phrases.en: He stayed and worked alone in a foreign land.
phrases.nuance_ko: '홀로'와 함께 쓰면 외로운 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 홀로, the lonely feeling becomes stronger.

explain_en: Compared with '외국' (foreign country), it carries feelings like loneliness and longing. It often appears in stories about people living away from home, and its counterparts are '고국' and '고향'. It's not used for simply talking about traveling abroad.

examples.en: Many relatives gathered at my grandmother's funeral home.
I prepared condolence money before going to the funeral home.
There is a funeral home next to the hospital.
I met my cousin at the funeral home after a long time.
It took thirty minutes by taxi to get to the funeral home.
A funeral home is a place where you need to be quiet.

explain: 한국 장례식장은 보통 병원 안이나 옆에 있어서 '병원 장례식장'이라고도 해요. 가면 검은색이나 어두운 옷을 입고 '조의금'을 내고 조문하는 게 일반적이에요. 인사는 '삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다'처럼 정중하게 해요.

phrases.en: My friend's father passed away, so I went to the funeral home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조문하러 갈 때 가장 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural phrase for going to pay respects.
phrases.en_equiv: to go to a funeral home

phrases.en: The hospital funeral home is close to my house, so it's convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국에서 흔한 장례식장 위치를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the common location of funeral homes in Korea.

phrases.en: You should speak quietly at a funeral home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'가 붙어 그 장소에서 지켜야 할 예절을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에서, often used when talking about manners there.

explain_en: Funeral homes in Korea are usually inside or next to a hospital, so people also say '병원 장례식장'. Visitors normally wear black or dark clothes, give '조의금' and pay their respects. The greeting is polite, like '삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다'.

examples.en: This bus's final stop is Seoul Station.
Please wake me when we reach the last stop.

examples.ko: 여행의 종착지가 어디인지 아직 정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: I haven't decided where the trip will end yet.
The train has almost reached its final stop.

examples.ko: 인생의 종착지가 어디일지 가끔 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Sometimes I wonder where life's final destination will be.

examples.ko: 이 지하철은 종착지까지 한 시간 넘게 걸려요.
examples.en: This subway takes over an hour to reach the last stop.

explain: 버스나 지하철에서는 '종점', '종착역'이라는 말을 더 많이 써요. '종착지'는 긴 여행이나 인생의 마지막 목적지처럼 비유로도 쓰기 좋아요. 반대말은 '출발지'예요.

phrases.en: Please get off at the last stop of this bus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스나 지하철에서 가장 흔하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word for the last stop on a bus or subway.

phrases.en: This train's final station is Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기차나 지하철의 마지막 역을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The last station of a train or subway.

phrases.en: He thinks of his hometown as the final destination of his life.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비유로 쓰면 삶의 마지막 목적지라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for the final destination of one's life.

explain_en: For buses and subways, '종점' and '종착역' are more common. '종착지' also works well as a metaphor for the end of a long journey or of life. Its opposite is '출발지' (starting point).

examples.en: There is a big plaza in the central part of the city.

examples.ko: 이 지도에서 중앙부는 빨간색으로 표시돼 있어요.
examples.en: On this map, the central area is marked in red.
The seats in the middle section of the hall are the most expensive.
The central part of the island is made up of mountains.

examples.ko: 다리 중앙부가 약해서 공사를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The middle of the bridge is weak, so they are doing repairs.
It plays when you press the middle of the screen.

explain: 중앙부는 '가운데'와 비슷하지만 설명문과 지도, 기사에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '가운데'나 '한가운데'라고 해요. 같은 식으로 '북부', '남부'처럼 '-부'가 붙으면 어떤 지역의 한 부분을 가리켜요.

phrases.en: There is a desk in the middle of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중앙부와 같은 뜻인데, 일상에서는 '가운데'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 중앙부, but 가운데 is much more natural in daily speech.

phrases.en: There is a fountain right in the middle of the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가운데'보다 정확히 중심인 곳을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes the exact center, more than 가운데.

phrases.en: The central part of the lake is deep.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중앙부 앞에 장소를 붙여서 그곳의 가운데 부분을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a place before 중앙부 to describe the central part of it.

explain_en: 중앙부 is close to '가운데' but is a stiff word used in explanations, maps and articles. In daily life people say '가운데' or '한가운데'. In the same way, '-부' in '북부' and '남부' marks one part of an area.

en: to land; to set down; to touch down

examples.en: The plane landed safely at Incheon Airport.
We are landing soon, so please fasten your seat belt.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 착륙할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the plane could not land.
I saw a photo of the spacecraft that landed on the moon.
The moment it landed, the passengers clapped.

examples.ko: 안개 때문에 다른 공항에 착륙해서 많이 늦었어요.
examples.en: We landed at a different airport because of fog, so we were very late.

explain: 반대말은 '이륙하다'예요. 사람이 비행기에서 나올 때는 '내리다'를 쓰고, 비행기가 땅에 닿을 때는 '착륙하다'를 써요. 우주선과 헬리콥터에도 쓰고, 'ㄱ'과 'ㄹ'이 만나는 소리 변화 때문에 '창뉴카다'로 발음해요.

phrases.en: The spaceship landed on the moon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기뿐 아니라 우주선이 땅에 내릴 때도 쓴다는 것을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: It shows the verb also works for spaceships, not only planes.

phrases.en: The flight attendant announced preparations for landing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '착륙'은 '준비'와 함께 안내 방송에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun often appears with '준비' in announcements.

phrases.example: 비행기가 이륙한 지 한 시간 됐어요.
phrases.en: It has been an hour since the plane took off.
phrases.nuance_ko: '착륙하다'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the opposite of '착륙하다'.

explain_en: Aircraft or spacecraft landing on the ground or runway. The opposite is 이륙하다. A person getting off a plane uses 내리다, while the plane touching the ground is 착륙하다. It also works for spacecraft and helicopters, and a sound change (ㄱ+ㄹ becomes ㅇ+ㄴ, and ㄱ+ㅎ becomes ㅋ) makes it pronounced 창뉴카다.

t90.ax: The plane landed safely at Incheon Airport.

examples.en: On the weekend, I went to an observatory with my family.

examples.ko: 큰 망원경이 있는 천문대로 소풍을 갔어요.
examples.en: We went on a trip to an observatory with a big telescope.

examples.ko: 산 위 천문대는 별이 잘 보여서 인기예요.
examples.en: The observatory on the mountain is popular because the stars are clear.
An observatory staff member explained the constellations.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 천문대에서 일하고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to work at an observatory since I was little.
When the observatory roof opens, you can see the sky.

explain: '과학관'은 전시를 보는 곳이고 '천문대'는 망원경으로 실제 하늘을 보는 곳이에요. 비슷한 말로 '관측소'가 있지만 일상에서는 '천문대'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '천문대에 가다', '천문대를 견학하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: Watching the stars at the observatory was really amazing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천문대의 가장 기본적인 쓰임이에요. 망원경으로 하늘을 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic use: looking at the sky through a telescope.
phrases.en_equiv: to see stars at the observatory

phrases.en: Tomorrow our school is going on an observatory field trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교나 단체가 배우러 방문할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a school or group visits to learn.

phrases.en: The observatory's telescope is really big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천문대에 있는 큰 망원경을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the large telescope at an observatory.

explain_en: A '과학관' is a place to see exhibits, while a '천문대' is where you view the real sky through a telescope. A similar word is '관측소', but in daily life '천문대' is far more common. People say '천문대에 가다' or '천문대를 견학하다'.

t90.ax: When the observatory roof opens, you can see the sky.

examples.en: Every evening I take a walk along the stream.
The cherry blossoms bloomed by the stream, so it was crowded.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 천변 쪽이라서 아침에 새소리가 들려요.
examples.en: My house is on the stream side, so I hear birds in the morning.

examples.ko: 천변 자전거 길에서는 속도를 줄여 주세요.
examples.en: Please slow down on the bike path by the stream.
Kids are playing and catching fish by the stream.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 천변 길을 통제해요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, they close off the road by the stream.

explain: '강변'이 큰 강가라면 '천변'은 작은 하천의 가장자리를 말해요. '○○천변'처럼 하천 이름 뒤에 붙여서도 써요. 산책길이나 자전거 길과 같이 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Walking along the stream on weekends feels good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 하천 가장자리를 따라 산책할 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for walking along the edge of a small stream.

phrases.en: There is a streamside walking path in front of my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하천을 따라 만들어진 걷는 길을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a walking path built along a stream.

phrases.en: Children ride bikes by the stream.
phrases.nuance_ko: '천변' 뒤에 조사 '에서'를 붙여 어디서 하는 일인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding the particle 에서 after 천변 tells where something is done.

explain_en: While '강변' is the bank of a big river, '천변' is the edge of a smaller stream. It can also be attached after a stream's name, like '○○천변'. It is often mentioned with walking paths and bike paths.

examples.ko: 산 위에 높은 철탑이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A tall steel tower stands on top of the mountain.

examples.ko: 철탑 위에서 작업하는 분들이 대단해 보여요.
examples.en: The people who work on top of the pylon look amazing.

examples.ko: 철탑을 따라 전깃줄이 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: Power lines stretch long along the pylons.
I can see pylons lined up in the distance.
A bird built a nest on the tall steel tower.

examples.ko: 논 가운데 철탑 몇 개가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A few steel towers stand in the middle of the rice fields.

explain: 쇠 구조물로 만든 높은 탑이에요. 전깃줄을 걸어 놓은 송전 철탑을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 관광용 탑은 보통 '타워'라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 들판에 송전 철탑이 줄지어 서 있어요.
phrases.en: Power transmission towers stand in a row across the field.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전깃줄을 걸어 둔 철탑을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to towers carrying power lines.

phrases.en: The worker climbed the tower wearing a safety line.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 철탑에 올라가 일하는 모습과 함께 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with scenes of working at height.

phrases.en: I can see a tall steel tower on the hill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 철탑의 높이를 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the tower's height.

explain_en: Modern metal tower for power lines or transmission (송전 철탑) It is a tall tower built from a steel structure, and often means a power transmission pylon holding up electric lines. Sightseeing towers are usually just called '타워'.

examples.ko: 국경 초소에서 군인이 경계를 서고 있어요.
examples.en: A soldier is standing guard at the border post.
There is a small guard post at the entrance of the mountain path.

examples.ko: 초소 앞에서 신분증을 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to show your ID in front of the checkpoint.

examples.ko: 아파트 입구 초소에 경비 아저씨가 계세요.
examples.en: A security guard is at the booth at the apartment entrance.

examples.ko: 초소 근무를 서는 병사가 밤새 깨어 있었어요.
examples.en: The soldier on guard duty stayed awake all night.

examples.ko: 낡은 초소는 이제 전망대로 쓰이고 있어요.
examples.en: The old guard post is now used as an observation deck.

explain: 군대나 경찰, 경비가 지키며 서는 작은 건물이나 장소예요. 아파트의 작은 방은 보통 '경비실'이라고 해요. '초소형 사이즈'의 초소는 한자가 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: The soldiers guarded the post all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 초소에서 경계를 서는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for standing guard at a post.

phrases.example: 차들이 검문 초소 앞에서 잠깐 멈췄어요.
phrases.en: The cars stopped briefly in front of the checkpoint.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지나가는 사람과 차를 확인하는 초소를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A post that checks people and vehicles passing through.

phrases.en: Please leave the package at the apartment security office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아파트나 건물의 작은 경비 장소는 보통 '경비실'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The small guard room in an apartment or building is usually called '경비실'.

explain_en: It is a small building or place where the military, police or guards keep watch. At apartment buildings, the small guard room is usually called '경비실'. The 초소 in '초소형 사이즈' (ultra-small size) is a different word with different Chinese characters.

examples.ko: 아들이 최전방 부대에서 군 복무를 해요.
examples.en: My son is serving in the army at a front-line unit.
A long fence stretches along the front line.
Medical staff worked on the front line of the response to the infectious disease.

examples.ko: 그는 판매 현장의 최전방에 서서 고객을 만나요.
examples.en: He stands at the front line of sales and meets customers.
It is hard for ordinary people to enter the front-line area.

examples.ko: 감독은 가장 빠른 선수를 최전방으로 올려 보냈어요.
examples.en: The coach sent his fastest player up to the front.

explain: 원래는 군대에서 적과 가장 가까운 곳을 가리키지만, 요즘은 '가장 앞에서 직접 부딪히는 자리'를 비유할 때도 써요. '전방'은 앞쪽 전체이고 '최전방'은 그중 맨 앞이에요. '최'가 '가장'의 뜻을 더해 줘요.

phrases.en: to work on the front line
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대가 아니어도 위험하거나 힘든 현장에서 가장 먼저 직접 일하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not only military: used for people doing the hardest, most direct work in a tough field.

explain_en: Literal military front; soldiers, borders. Originally 최전방 means the place in the military closest to the enemy, but now it is also used figuratively for the spot that faces problems head-on. 전방 is the whole forward area, and 최전방 is the very front of it. The 최 adds the sense of 'most'.

en: departure of a ship from port; setting sail

examples.en: The ship's departure was canceled because of the typhoon.
The departure time is nine in the morning.
The fog was thick, so they postponed the departure by a day.

examples.ko: 오늘 출항은 바람이 강해서 어려울 것 같아요.
examples.en: Setting sail today seems difficult because the wind is strong.

examples.ko: 첫 출항 때 느낀 설렘을 아직도 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: I still can't forget the excitement I felt on my first voyage out.

examples.ko: 출항 전에 안전 점검을 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.en: You must do a safety check before setting sail.

explain: 배가 항구를 떠날 때 쓰는 말이라 일반적인 '출발'과 달라요. 반대말은 '입항'이고, 날씨 때문에 배가 못 뜰 때 '출항 금지', '출항 취소'라는 말이 뉴스에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The ship leaves port early in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '출항'의 동사형으로 배가 항구를 떠난다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '출항', meaning a ship leaves port.

phrases.en: Because of strong wind, a ban on sailing was issued.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 나쁠 때 배가 못 떠나게 하는 조치로 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often in the news for when bad weather stops ships from leaving.

phrases.en: The sailors are preparing to set sail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 떠나기 전에 준비하는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for preparing before a ship departs.

explain_en: A ship departs from a harbor. It is used when a ship leaves port, so it differs from the general word '출발' (departure). Its opposite is '입항', and phrases like '출항 금지' and '출항 취소' often appear in the news when weather keeps ships in.

examples.en: Small fishing boats came into the harbor.
On the weekend I visited a small harbor on the West Sea.
I ate raw fish at a restaurant near the harbor.

examples.ko: 이 포구는 해 질 무렵이 제일 예뻐요.
examples.en: This harbor is prettiest around sunset.
The fishermen left the harbor at dawn.
The harbor village has many quiet alleys.

explain: '항구'보다 작고 정겨운 바닷가 마을 느낌이 있어요. 큰 배가 오가는 곳은 '항구', 어선이 드나드는 작은 곳은 '포구'라고 해요. 여행 글에서 '포구 마을'이라는 말을 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: I ate fresh fish in a small harbor village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행 글에서 자주 보는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often seen in travel writing.

phrases.example: 우리는 바다 옆 작은 포구에서 쉬었어요.
phrases.en: We rested at a small harbor by the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포구가 원래 작은 항구라서 '작은'과 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits well with 작은 since a 포구 is already a small port.

phrases.en: The boat arrived at the harbor in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배가 들어오거나 도착하는 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the place where a boat arrives.

explain_en: Small, cozy coastal harbor, often fishing, literary tone. Compared with 항구, 포구 feels smaller and more homey. A big ship port is a 항구, while a small place for fishing boats is a 포구. In travel writing you often see the phrase 포구 마을.

examples.en: The time we agreed on has already passed.

examples.ko: 계약한 지 일 년이 경과하면 값이 바뀌어요.
examples.en: Once a year has passed since the contract, the price changes.

examples.ko: 수술 후 시간이 경과할수록 몸이 나아졌어요.
examples.en: As time passed after the surgery, my body got better.
Throw away milk that is past its expiration date.

examples.ko: 신청 기간이 경과해서 접수할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The application period has passed, so we can't accept it.

examples.ko: 두 시간이 경과하고 나서야 연락이 왔어요.
examples.en: The call came only after two hours had passed.

explain: 시간이 지나가거나, 정해진 기간이 넘었다는 것을 서류나 안내문에서 딱딱하게 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '지나다', '지나가다'를 더 많이 써요. 기한이 이미 끝났다는 느낌이 들어서 '기한이 경과하다' 같은 표현이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The appointment time has already passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가장 자연스러운 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural everyday word with the same meaning.

phrases.example: 신청 기한이 경과해서 접수할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: The application deadline has passed, so we can't accept it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 기한이 이미 끝났다고 딱딱하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices to formally say a deadline has already passed.

phrases.example: 이사한 지 아직 한 달이 경과하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: A month has not yet passed since I moved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 기간이 아직 안 됐다는 뜻으로 서류에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the set period has not yet passed and often appears in documents.

explain_en: A stiff, written-style way to say time has passed or a set period has run out, common in notices and documents. In daily conversation Koreans prefer 지나다 or 지나가다. It often carries the feeling that a deadline is already over, as in 기한이 경과하다.

dis.h: formal verb for elapsed time or a period
gh: time goes by; everyday basic word
passive form; a period has run out

p.n: 지나다 is plainer and more everyday.

t90.ax: The time we agreed on has already passed.

examples.ko: 지금은 과도기적 단계라서 규칙이 자주 바뀌어요.
examples.en: We're in a transitional stage now, so the rules change often.
Confusion easily arises in a transitional situation.
This system is only a transitional measure.

examples.ko: 새 시스템으로 바꾸는 과도기적 기간에는 두 방식을 같이 써요.
examples.en: During the transitional period of switching to the new system, we use both methods.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 지금 과도기적 변화를 겪고 있어요.
examples.en: Our company is going through a transitional change right now.

examples.ko: 과도기적 모습이 보이지만 곧 안정될 거예요.
examples.en: It looks transitional, but it will settle down soon.

explain: '과도기적 단계/상황/조치'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여서 써요. 서술할 때는 '지금은 과도기예요'처럼 '과도기'를 쓰는 게 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: We're in a transitional stage now, so it's a bit inconvenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변하는 중간 시기를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for an in-between period of change.

phrases.en: The government announced a transitional measure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 제도가 자리 잡기 전에 임시로 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to temporary steps before a new system settles.

phrases.en: Our company is in a transition period now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서술할 때는 '과도기'를 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For predicate use, use '과도기' like this.

explain_en: It goes before a noun, as in '과도기적 단계/상황/조치'. As a predicate, saying '지금은 과도기예요' using '과도기' sounds more natural.
